#4533. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4532. Gift Guide: Best Tech and Gadgets for Gearheads and Car Lovers

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

Keep up with the latest automotive and garage tech with our picks for the best gadgets and tech on the market today.

This article was updated in November 2026.

Automotive enthusiasm has always gone hand in hand with a fascination for technology. At Road & Track, we’re always interested in the technology that makes the automotive experience better.

Some are practical necessities, others are just plain cool, but each has something to offer a car enthusiast. Think diagnostic scanners, GPS navigation systems, performance monitors, wireless phone accessories, and clever tools that help tackle jobs around the garage.

We’ve included options at various price points and for different kinds of enthusiasts, so you can find something useful, interesting, and worth keeping in the toolbox.

The Mission 1 Pro is built for capturing the kind of driving footage that makes you want to take the long way home. I recently used one myself on a drive up the Pacific Coast Highway, where its compact size made it easy to bring along and its high-resolution video captured everything from sweeping coastal views to the little details along the road. It’s a versatile action camera for car enthusiasts who want more than a few phone clips from their next road trip, with the rugged, portable design GoPro has built its reputation on.

The Cobra RAD 700i is less a radar detector and more a digital co-pilot for the fast lane. With long-range detection, GPS-powered AutoLearn filtering, and Bluetooth connectivity to Cobra’s Drive Smarter network, it helps cut through false alerts while keeping you tuned into live speed traps, cameras, and roadside hazards. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility sweeten the deal, turning your windshield into mission control for highway miles and heavy right feet.

A navigation app is only as useful as the cellular connection behind it, and that can become a problem once you get far enough outside town. The weBoost Drive X is a multi-user cellular signal booster that uses an external magnetic-mount antenna to capture available signals, then amplifies them for devices inside the cabin. Its amplifier delivers up to 50 dB of gain and supports several major U.S. cellular frequency bands. The kit includes both exterior and interior antennas, a power supply, and the amplifier itself, making it a worthwhile consideration for road trippers, overlanders, and anyone who regularly ventures beyond reliable cell coverage.

Running navigation, streaming music, and charging wirelessly can turn a smartphone into a little pocket-size space heater, especially on a summer road trip. Pioneer’s SDA-SC600 combines a magnetic Qi2 charging mount with an integrated cooling fan designed to help manage device temperatures during longer drives. It supports wireless charging at up to 15 watts, includes an adjustable air-vent mount, and uses a multicolor LED indicator to show charging status.

A phone running Google Maps isn’t going to cut it when the pavement ends and the trail network gets complicated. The Garmin Tread 2 Overland Edition is an eight-inch, glove-friendly GPS navigator built specifically for off-road travel, with preloaded topographic maps of North and South America, public-land information, and U.S. Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Maps. Its IP67-rated enclosure is designed to withstand dust, water exposure, and rough conditions, while the included magnetic-assisted locking mount secures the unit to the dashboard. It also supports downloadable satellite imagery and route planning through Garmin’s Tread app, giving overlanders a much more capable navigation setup than a smartphone alone.

If you're serious about reverse-engineering custom car parts or replicating impossible-to-find trim pieces, a high-quality 3D scanner is a garage game-changer. The Creality Sermoon P1 takes the clunky laptop out of the equation by packing an advanced blue-laser and NIR structured-light scanner into a standalone, tetherless device. With a built-in 6-inch touchscreen and powerful onboard processing, you can scan, mesh, and export digital models of engine bays or body panels directly from the unit without tripping over cables. It delivers metrology-grade 0.02mm accuracy, features a single-line laser mode to effortlessly capture deep holes and bolt recesses, and handles shiny metal or dark automotive plastics without requiring messy matte spray.

The BlueDriver Bluetooth Pro OBD2 Scanner is a compact diagnostic tool that plugs into a vehicle’s OBD-II port and sends information wirelessly to an iOS or Android device. Beyond reading and clearing standard check-engine codes, it offers enhanced diagnostics for systems such as ABS, airbags, transmission, and TPMS on supported vehicles. The companion app also provides live sensor data, Mode 6 test results, and repair reports with possible causes and reported fixes. With compatibility covering most 1996-and-newer North American vehicles and no subscription fees, it’s a useful step up from a basic code reader for anyone who likes doing their own troubleshooting.

A stopwatch can tell you whether your last lap was faster, but it won’t explain why. The Garmin Catalyst is a dedicated track-driving analysis system that combines a 10Hz multi-GNSS receiver, onboard accelerometers and gyroscopes, and an HD remote camera to record and evaluate a driver’s performance. Garmin’s True Track Positioning technology analyzes racing lines, braking points, apexes, and track-out positions, while its True Optimal Lap feature combines the best sections of recorded laps to show how much time is potentially left on the table. It can also deliver real-time audio coaching, making it a particularly interesting tool for track-day drivers who want to improve without investing in a complicated professional data-logging setup.

DJI’s Mini 4 Pro is packed full of impressive imaging capabilities and innovative navigation features. The 249-gram weight of the unit means the device is just under the Federal Aviation Administration’s 250-gram limit for registering your drone in the United States, significantly reducing the barriers to entry other drones require. The Mini 4 Pro captures 4K video at up to 100 frames per second (fps) or 4K at 60 fps with HDR video. The unit is rated for roughly 12 miles of transmission between the drone and the included remote, ensuring even congested areas or valleys/hills won’t impact your ability to record video or snap photos. Other features include 360-degree obstacle-avoidance sensors, a plethora of automated capture modes capable of locking in on and tracking subjects, and a 34-minute flight time with the included batteries.

Stop stuffing your pockets with multiple flashlights when you really just need this one. Holding the ArkPro Ultra feels immediately different than a standard flashlight; the flat, slim profile disappears in your pocket or EDC bag unlike bulky round tubes, yet the unibody aluminum feels incredibly dense and premium in the hand. It solves the biggest headache of carrying high-tech gear: charging anxiety. Because it finally supports both magnetic snap-charging and standard USB-C, you can top it off on your nightstand or with a laptop cable without hunting for a proprietary cord. Whether you are running a presentation or checking for leaks under a car, it feels like the Swiss Army knife of light that actually performs as well as the dedicated tools it replaces.

The IntelliDash Pro X10 is a modern shortcut for aging dashboards—a slim 10-inch touchscreen that brings wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto to just about any car without surgery, swearing, or a weekend in the garage. Setup is gloriously plug-and-play, with Bluetooth, FM, AUX, and voice-assistant support baked in. Big maps, brighter road trips, cleaner cable chaos. It’s the kind of upgrade that makes a 2009 commuter vehicle feel a little more spaceship.

A shiny new paint job can hide a lot of history, particularly on an older car that’s been through a few owners and at least one body shop. The Rdinscos Car Coating Thickness Meter is designed to measure the thickness of paint and other coatings on metal panels, giving buyers a way to compare readings across a vehicle’s bodywork. Uneven measurements can point toward previous refinishing, additional layers of paint, or body filler, making the tool particularly useful when inspecting a potential project or evaluating a used-car purchase. It’s not a replacement for a trained eye or a proper pre-purchase inspection, but it can help uncover evidence of repairs that a quick walkaround might miss.

The Hoto Tools Precision Screwdriver Kit Pro is a wonderful gift for any DIY aficionado or professional. The screwdriver uses a two-gear design to provide more than enough torque for delicate builds or repairs. It also features built-in LED lights and an innovative contact charging case that stores the drill and its accessories, ensuring power is always topped off when needed.

This kit isn’t just about looks—it’s about substance, with 48 bits forged from S2 steel, complemented by a suite of practical tools like spudgers, tweezers, and a suction cup for those tricky parts. The electric screwdriver’s adjustable torque and handy magnetizer/demagnetizer tool help to ensure no small bits and pieces go missing. Whether you’re a tech enthusiast or a creative tinkerer, the Hoto Tools kit provides practicality and precision in a compact, stylish package.

Built for gloveboxes, road trips, and “oh no” moments, the Vantrue JS3 is a compact four-in-one roadside powerhouse: jump starter, air compressor, fast-charging power bank, and emergency light, in one rugged shell. With a 3250-amp peak current, 160-psi inflator, and USB-C PD 65-watt charging, it’s designed to revive dead batteries, refill tires fast, and keep devices alive when the highway gets unpredictable. Think of it as roadside insurance with a lithium heartbeat.

Shopping for someone who already has every gadget is tough, but the Insta360 X6 is a guaranteed win. Because it shoots in every direction at once, you don’t even have to worry about framing—just hit record and pick the best angles later on your phone. The software automatically edits out the selfie stick, making it look like a low-flying drone is following you, whether you’re carving up back roads, hitting the mountain bike trails, or just messing around in the backyard. It’s incredibly easy to use and makes literally any activity look epic.

Reverse-engineering a custom intake manifold or replicating a classic car’s unobtainium trim pieces usually means dragging a fragile laptop into the grime of the garage. The Creality Sermoon P1 standalone 3-D scanner finally severs that tether. This isn’t some plastic hobbyist toy; it’s a high-octane engineering workstation crammed into a handheld chassis. Packing a Qualcomm 8-core processor and a massive 24GB of RAM, the P1 processes dense 3-D meshes directly on its crisp six-inch touchscreen. It boasts enough onboard horsepower to digitize a complete engine block without breaking a single drop of digital sweat. For the uncompromising gearhead looking to turn physical metal into flawless digital data, the Sermoon P1 is the ultimate garage weapon.

This cordless four-in-one Slim V8 Apex mini vacuum packs 19,000Pa suction into a glovebox-friendly frame, with attachments for crumbs, cupholders, keyboards, pet hair, and other chaos agents. It also blows, inflates, and pumps, making it equal parts detail tool and travel sidekick. Lightweight, USB-C rechargeable, and surprisingly mighty, it’s built for people who treat messes like pit stops—not permanent conditions.

The Nextmug Go is the kind of gadget that quietly upgrades your entire morning ritual. This sleek, self-heating travel mug keeps coffee or tea at your preferred temperature — Warm, Hot, or Piping — for hours, so every sip tastes freshly poured. Its spill-resistant lid, long-lasting battery, and app-free controls make it refreshingly simple to use on commutes, road trips, or marathon workdays. Think of it as a thermos with a master’s degree in modern convenience.

HoverAir’s X1 ProMax is the ultimate drone for people who don’t know anything about drones. This self-flying, fully enclosed camera launches from your hand and uses 10+ AI-powered shooting and follow modes to capture photographs and up to 8K/30 (or 4K/120) video, stabilized by SmoothCapture 2.0—a two-axis gimbal with electronic image stabilization (EIS) and horizon leveling. It’ll track confidently with a rated 42 km/h (26 mph) follow speed, and its OmniTerrain feature is designed for flying near water, snow, and other tricky surfaces. I’ve shot various drones over the years, and while others might be more technically capable, none are as simple to use as the ProMax. The best part is, it’ll fit nearly anywhere. It’s a no-brainer for anyone who wants to capture drone footage quickly in a device that folds up smaller than most books.

Ride1Up’s Revv 1 DRT is a moped-style e-bike that trades Lycra vibes for dirt-track energy. A 52-volt system feeds a 1000-watt Bafang rear hub and a 35-amp controller with a “boost” party trick, while a 52-vole/20-Ah UL-certified pack (about 1040 watt-hours) keeps the lights on. Off-road mode unlocks 28-plus mph for private property, and the chassis gets real hardware: a 150-mm dual-crown fork, 76 mm of rear travel, and flur-piston hydraulic stoppers. Range is quoted at 30–60 miles, and the whole package carries UL 2849/2271 safety certifications—welcome peace of mind on a 30-mph pseudo-moto.

On trail or torn-up alleys, the DRT feels like a small, electric pit bike: confident, quick to squirt, and more fun than it has any right to be. The flip side is familiar: short cranks and moped geometry make real pedaling an afterthought, knobby 20-by-fours hum and nibble at range, and you’ll want to mind local laws before touching that off-road setting. At $2395, it undercuts many fashion-forward rivals while delivering genuine off-road chops and useful kit (headlight fairing, molle mounting, twist throttle). If your commute occasionally turns to dirt, this is the hooligan commuter to beat.

#4531. World’s first ‘dark magic mushroom’ discovered in Florida

Published Nov 12, 2026 11:59 AM EST

A mushroom recently discovered in Florida looks unassuming, but this fungus

packs a serious and surprising punch. According to mycologists writing in the journal Current Biology, Galerina indica is the first-known “dark magic mushroom,” a species featuring hefty doses of both psychedelic and poisonous compounds.

Depending on their chemical makeup, many mushrooms will do one of two things. Fungi packed with psilocybin can send users on an extensive psychedelic trip, while varieties laden with amatoxins can be poisonous. Although mycologists have long assumed a single species could hypothetically feature both traits, no one had ever documented such an example. A recent field survey changed that, however.

“I could hardly believe it. We knew it was possible, but tried not to get too excited until we did a more rigorous analysis,” Andrew Kunik, a former University of Florida plant pathologist and study co-author, said in a statement.

Evolutionary biologists suspect certain mushrooms developed their poisonous amatoxins as a protection against foraging animals, although hallucinogenic psilocybin’s emergence and purpose in fungi remains unclear. Regardless, both compounds found their way into G. indica. University of Utah mycologist and study co-author Bryn Dentinger believes that a process called horizontal gene transfer is likely to blame—although it’s a completely novel discovery.

“Horizontal gene transfer is like if we shook hands and some of my DNA incorporated into your genome,” he said. “[But] two independent horizontal gene transfer events for these specialized metabolites in one mushroom genus are unheard of.”

For as unique as G. indica is, it is very easy to miss. The small, innocuous brown mushrooms are barely the size of a thumbnail, and resemble countless other fungi.

“These mushrooms are really hard to find,” added study co-author, University of Florida plant pathologist, and state mycologist Matthew Smith. “It’s hard to differentiate them from others, even for a trained expert.”

Although difficult, documenting the specimens is not only vital to the field of mycology. It can help save lives.

“Part of my job as Florida’s state mycologist is to identify poisonous or potentially poisonous species,” explained Smith. “So it is important to know what species we have and whether they might cause problems for people or pets.”

#4530. Garmin and Waze just teamed up on a clever new way to keep cyclists safer

Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting new safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

The new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.

I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

That’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a big difference.

Of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

The feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin says location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Big Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

This is cool but requires both a Garmin product and the Waze app. IMHO better to equip new cars and trucks with bicycle and pedestrian detection.

Garmin LiveTrack itself is free for users with compatible Garmin devices and previously allowed cyclists to share their live location, speed, route, and other information with friends and family. I’ve used it myself as a safety feature when venturing off-road and on longer solo journeys. The Waze integration essentially expands that safety net to nearby motorists.

There’s obviously one big limitation: You need to be riding with a compatible Garmin device, and the driver needs to be using Waze.

But with Waze claiming around 200 million users globally and Garmin being one of the biggest names in cycling computers and fitness watches, that’s not exactly a tiny Venn diagram.

Anything that gives drivers another chance to see cyclists before actually seeing them sounds like a win to me.

#4529. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4528. Honda Investing $3 Billion to Build New Ohio Factory, Increase Hybrid Production in U.S.

The new plant will be capable of producing 240,000 vehicles a year, and multiple new models are currently under development.

Audi may have recently announced its first-ever U.S. production facility, but at least one Japanese automaker with a head start in that race doesn’t seem keen on giving up any places. On Monday, Honda announced it is investing $3 billion in a new central Ohio factory; the plant, which will produce up to 240,000 vehicles annually, is expected to be online by 2029.

Now, with nine production facilities across the U.S., Honda is no stranger to domestic production, but the new factory plan goes beyond merely adding production capacity. Instead, the company is targeting increased production of hybrid-electric vehicles and their accompanying drivetrain parts. The new plant will sit between Honda’s current East Liberty and Marysville Auto Plants, the carmaker said, and will focus on multiple vehicle types and powertrains, including hybrid and battery-electric vehicles. Honda said the plant will be one of the most advanced factories in the world, leveraging leading-edge automation, data-driven technologies and flexible production systems.

"As Honda approaches 50 years of building products close to our customers in America, we are making one of the most significant commitments in our history to position Honda for the next 50 years,” said Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “These investments strengthen America’s role as a cornerstone of Honda’s global future and reflect our confidence in our more than 30,000 Honda associates and the strength of American manufacturing. By expanding our comprehensive R&D and manufacturing capabilities, we will be better positioned to serve our customers and contribute to the economic vitality of the communities where we operate.”

Building another plant in Ohio was an easy choice for Honda. Honda’s U.S. supply base is nearby, and the automaker has a strong reputation among the region’s skilled workforce. The Japanese automaker has previously committed to launching 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030; North America is the target for many of these models, which are currently in development at R&D facilities in California and Ohio. All told, Honda said the new plant will increase its annual U.S. production capacity to approximately 1.3 million vehicles a year.

The company’s Alabama Auto Plant will also receive new investment to expand engine production for a new V-6 hybrid engine; Honda will retool the engine production facility and one of the production lines to accommodate Passport SUV production. The Anna Engine Plant in Ohio will also be retooled, to produce a next-generation 4-cylinder Atkinson-cycle engine for future compact and midsize vehicles built in North America. Honda Transmission Plant-Ohio will be retooled for two next-generation Honda Hybrid systems in compact vehicles, while Honda Transmission Plant-Georgia will be retooled for next-generation hybrid systems in larger vehicles. All this retooling will account for a 250-percent increase in hybrid powertrain system capacity in Ohio.

“Honda's leadership could have chosen to build this plant anywhere in the world, but they chose Ohio because there are so many advantages to being here,” said Ohio governor Mike DeWine. “For almost half a century, Honda and Ohio have grown together, and generations of families have built their careers on Honda's manufacturing lines. Today's announcement isn't just an investment in a new facility—it's an investment in Ohio's people and Ohio's future.”

A New York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

#4527. Robotic slugs with claws can fuse together to create one massive machine

Published Nov 12, 2026 1:07 PM EST

An unsuspecting traveler trucking their way through a hiking trail would likely stop in bewilderment if they saw it: a nearly two-foot-long, Slinky-like contraption made of plastic and rubber, clambering forward like an inchworm. That confusion would shift to unease when scanning up and down its bendy, elephant-trunk-like body and seeing pairs of snapping claws at either end. Unabashed horror would inevitably take over as our traveler watches another one of the soulless Slinkies appear, inch toward the first one, and connect at the claws, creating one much larger, lifeless wiggly slug. All around, more clawed robots would close in from the forest and merge until they’d combined into a lizard-like mishmash of plastic and claws the size of a small bear.

These clawed robots are, in fact, real and they are the latest creation coming from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Colorado State University. Inspired by the unique, flexible strength of elephant trunks, the 3D-printed TeCoBots robots are an attempt to work around the  usual rigid constraints of building a robot. The team used an approach called tensegrity, in which the cylindrical rods in the robot’s body are held in place by a web of tensioned cables rather than rigidly locked together. This makes it bendy, like a Slinky, so it can twist and turn around obstacles or collapse down on itself. In testing, a remote human operator was able to use the robot’s bendy body and gripper claws on either of its ends to traverse over a large branch outdoors. It can also roll over itself repeatedly, shimmy up a pipe, and slither like a snake.

But as our unfortunate hypothetical hiker discovered, TeCoBot really shines when it works with others. Engineers designed the robots so that their claws can grasp onto another robot and merge. These modular robot links can move as one or operate independently of each other to complete more complicated tasks. In the study and accompanying videos, gaggles of chained TeCoBots work together to climb up a desk and grab a pen, open a sealed jar, or grab an object and carry it across a room. All of this, the researchers emphasize, has humanity’s best interest at heart. The robot’s flexible design could make them invaluable tools in search and rescue missions where they could squeeze into places rescuers can’t reach. One day, these teams of robotic slugs may work together to accomplish tasks unsuited for humans on spacecraft and extraterrestrial planets.

“In the future, we can envision mostly autonomous teams of tens or even hundreds of them – attached through the claws—traveling to a location and then deploying for a specific purpose,” Colorado State University Associate Professor Jianguo Zhao said in a statement. “They are very adaptable to the situation and goals.”

Details of the robot were published this week in the journal Nature Machine Intelligence.

Zhao and his colleagues started the project to fill some of the gaps in current robot hardware. Though many new types of machines are being built these days, most are still made from sturdy but rigid materials that limit their flexibility. Most robots also tend to prioritize either locomotion (moving) or manipulation (grabbing stuff), with few excelling at both.

Like most human problems, nature already devised a solution long ago. In this case, the researchers looked to the remarkable combination of strength and flexibility in an elephant’s trunk. These marvels of evolution let the world’s largest land mammals both heft rocks weighing several hundred pounds and gently peel open bananas. That wide range and adaptability could come in handy for a robot.

The device they ended up creating measured one foot 11 inches long, has a 4.3-inch diameter and weighs around 600 grams (1.3 pounds) without batteries, roughly the same as a fully loaded Italian sub. Each robot module is made of six carbon fiber rods and a continuous, stretchable, 3D-printed tension. This stretchy and bendy design means one robot can bend either direction, stretch up like an accordion or collapse down on itself.

The claws at either end of TeCoBot are fundamental to how it can combine with its fellow slinky-bots. The grippers connect and lock onto each other, reducing the need for other connectors like magnets, which are more prone to mechanical failure. Once connected, each robot can offload certain physical stresses to the others to lighten its load, giving the whole system what the research team refers to as a kind of “embodied intelligence.”

Working together, these linked robots can complete far more complicated tasks than any one of them could alone. In demonstration videos, the robots roll towards each other and connect to form one long robot that can more easily loop around a pipe. In another example, several more robots combine to form an H-shape, which then allows the entity to climb along a duct. The merged robots are still able to use the unlined claws at either end to precisely grab objects. The team demonstrated this by instructing a multi-robot TeCoBot chain to climb a desk, pluck a pen out of a container with its claw, crawl back down to the ground, and drop the pen into a trash can.

“They can bend around to lift and carry different sized objects with their body or to navigate difficult terrain like a snake would,” Zhao said.

This actually isn’t the first time roboticists have turned to elephants for design choices. A previous entry called EleTac from a team out of Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology replaced the main sensors and camera normally in a robot grippers with essentially one massive integrated sensor able to “feel” an object’s texture. That approach, mirroring an elephant’s tactile trunk, resulted in a gripper that could hold a sponge and wipe down dirty plates and blindly feel for a pen buried beneath a layer of sand.

Meanwhile, another team from the University of Hong Kong,created their own Aerial Elephant Trunk robot grippers and strapped them to the sides of flying drones, essentially giving them a floppy, grippy tail. Real samples of elephant trunk skin tissue have also been studied and used as a reference point for  new surface material that could be used to make  soft robots that are similarly tough and durable on one end but flexible and sensitive on the other.

#4526. The new BMW i3 just proved how efficient an EV can be after a nearly 3,700-mile road trip

Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

The Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the new i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse

BMW said the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The new i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW said the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s new i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the new i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW said the new 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

With an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

Very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

Like the new iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The new BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.

#4525. Stolen McLaren 750S Spotted Doing Donuts at Detroit Street Takeover, Tracked Down Via Social Media

The McLaren's owner put his 1.1 million followers to work tracking down his purloined supercar.

If you’re going to steal a bright green McLaren 750S, you might want to try to keep a low profile. At least, as low a profile as can be possible in a supercar. Doing donuts at a street takeover in front of a crowd of spectators, then, is probably not the best idea.

According to ClickOnDetroit, this indeed happened. The McLaren in question belonged to Ali Sobh, a Detroit businessman and social media influencer with approximately 1.1 million followers. The exotic car was reportedly stolen from a driveway behind his home in Detroit's historic Boston-Edison neighborhood. Sobh was understandably upset when he realized his prized possession was taken; however, salt arrived in the wound when he saw a video circulating online showing his McLaren spinning donuts in front of spectators, many of whom were recording the spectacle on their phones.

So, Sobh turned to his social media followers for help locating the McLaren. Tips began coming in, eventually providing a possible location near Six Mile Road and Telegraph Road. Sobh passed that information along to Detroit police, who subsequently recovered the car.

Getting the McLaren back is obviously a big win, but that’s not the end of the story. Detroit police are reviewing footage from the street takeover and working to identify those responsible for the theft. Authorities have not announced any arrests, and it's unclear whether the person performing donuts was involved in stealing the vehicle.

Sobh claims his car is worth approximately $500,000, and he doesn’t ever want it stolen again, so he says plans to improve security around his home to prevent that from happening. In the meantime, it must be reassuring to know that he can count on more than one million followers to help him out when things go south.

#4524. Dragon boy Durin is the star of the show in Genshin Impact's wintry Luna 3 update, launching in early December

Genshin Impact is getting two new characters and a whole host of new content in Version Luna 3, which arrives in under two weeks.

The latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain new powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

#4522. John F. Kennedy Jr.’s Last Car, a 1994 Saab 900 Coupe, Is Going Up for Auction

And, yes, in case you were wondering, it is a five-speed manual.

If you’ve ever wanted to own an automotive piece of Kennedy family history, now’s your chance. John F. Kennedy Jr.’s last car, a 1994 Saab 900 SE Coupe, will be auctioned off Wednesday, November 11th at 7 p.m. EST by RR Auctions.

The dark green three-door coupe was the last vehicle Kennedy owned before he, his wife Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, and sister-in-law Lauren Bessette were killed in a plane crash off the coast of Martha’s Vineyard on July 16, 1999. As he purchased it new, Kennedy was able to have the Saab fitted with a light beige leather interior, a five-speed manual transmission, and a turquoise-green “Main Beach” roof rack. There’s only 30,650 miles on the odometer, and RR Auctions says the vehicle shows evidence of age and use, including wear on the leather upholstery and areas of soiling on the carpeting. A printed photograph of John F. Kennedy Jr. and Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy beside the Saab will be included.

“For a man born into one of America’s wealthiest and most famous families, Kennedy’s choice of a Saab was notably modest. He purchased the new 900 SE from Zumbach Sports Cars in Manhattan in the summer of 1994 for $29,841.21, equipped with such everyday conveniences as a CD player and phone hookup,” the listing reads. “The practical Swedish hatchback suited the understated, slightly unconventional style Kennedy cultivated as an adult, far removed from the ostentation his wealth and celebrity could have afforded him. He drove it regularly around New York, and the intensely photographed nature of his life made the Saab a recurring backdrop to his final years: numerous period images show Kennedy, and later Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, with the car, sometimes attempting to make their way through the paparazzi who followed them through the city.”

The Saab sat at the Larchmont, New York home of Kennedy’s friend, Kevin Hynes, for days after the plane crash. Hynes bought the Saab from the Kennedy estate in 2000 for $6000; in 2006, Hynes sold the 900 Coupe to Michael Esposito for $12,000.

When the vehicle was photographed on July 23, 1999, its contents included a football, a soccer ball, a rope, automotive fluid, a March 1999 issue of Rolling Stone, and a Piper baseball cap. Some of these items have been auctioned off previously, but this is the first time the vehicle itself has appeared. An E-ZPass transponder, a handwritten telephone-message sheet, an Airborne Express receipt associated with the 2000 estate transaction, and a DeWitt Stern Group envelope addressed to “Mr. John F. Kennedy” and marked “PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL” will be included with the purchase.

As of publication, 24 bids have been placed on the 1994 Saab 900. The current bidding price is $26,575.

A New York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

#4521. Dream Driving Experiences Make the Perfect Gift for Auto Enthusiasts

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

Give them something they'll never forget. From budget experiences to luxury excursions, there's a dream driving experience for every driver no matter the occasion.

This article was updated in November 2026.

Auto enthusiasts are notoriously difficult to shop for. Most already have their own tools, collectibles, garage décor, and driving gadgets, and they’re very particular about all of it. They've probably spent hours researching exactly which version they want. Good luck to anyone trying to buy them something last-minute.

It stands to reason, then, that the best gift for a car lover might be an opportunity to actually get behind the wheel.

Whether it's thrashing an exotic supercar around a famous track, honing their skills through professional instruction, tackling rugged terrain in an off-roader, chasing the Northern Lights by snowmobile, wafting over Europe's greatest roads in a luxurious grand tourer, or strapping into an actual race car for a full-speed ride-along, these experiences offer something every car enthusiast longs for—more time in the seat. The vehicles may differ, but the result is the same—a memory they'll be cherishing long after the holidays have passed.

Best of all, many of these driving experiences are offered as gift certificates or gift cards, which makes them excellent for last-minute gifting. E-vouchers from gifting sites are more versatile and far more personalized—and usually way more affordable—than pricier branded experiences from manufacturers. Your favorite driver can select their own driving vacation on their own schedule at locations around the world.

Got a car lover that's hard to buy for? Here's what we recommend, any time of year.

Virgin Gifts is another gifting site that sells e-vouchers for experiences, so your favorite driver can reserve their ultimate driving experience at their convenience. It's a great last-minute gift idea.

Our pick? BMW Performance Driving Experiences at official BMW proving grounds in either Greer, South Carolina, or Thermal, California (near Palm Springs). At the M Driving School, your favorite Bimmer lover will learn how to drive the legendary M line from professional drivers. They'll slip into the driver's seat of multiple M cars and conquer low- and high-speed driving exercises such as a slalom course and autocross, as well as a wet skidpad for drifting. Once they've mastered each course, they'll compete in timed runs against other drivers. The High-Performance Driver School is the same but with a wider variety of cars and experiences. The Teen Driver School is a fantastic option for young Bimmer fans to learn the basics.

Drive with us! Road & Track Experiences offers several opportunities each year to tour and explore a variety of locales around the U.S. You and a guest will join R&T editors for luxurious and leisurely rallies. Show off your most prized vehicles to like-minded enthusiasts, all while driving legendary roads in beautiful areas, staying in top-notch hotels, and eating at the finest restaurants.

In 2027, the Palm Canyon Run will explore the California Desert in late February, from Palm Springs and Joshua Tree to track time at Chuckwalla, as desert flowers bloom and temperatures are moderate and comfortable. In May, join us for a one-of-a-kind trip through New England, including the famous Kancamagus!

Got a trip to Las Vegas planned? Get out of the casino and onto the racetrack! Give your favorite car lover the chance to drive the world’s largest and fastest selection of Lamborghinis, Ferraris, Porsches, and more at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.

Tinggly is an aggregate gifting site that offers dozens of driving experiences from reputable services all over the world. Most Tinggly gifts are offered as gift e-cards; that means your favorite car lover can choose any experience they desire anywhere they want and on their own schedule. Even if driving exotic cars on a racetrack isn't their cup of tea, there's something at Tinggly that's guaranteed to get their motor running.

If your favorite auto enthusiast has impeccable taste for the finest, Huntermoss is the ultimate gift. Huntermoss (formerly Ultimate Driving Tours) curates luxurious tours and driving experiences in exotic supercars that celebrate passion for motoring and an appreciation for the finer things in life. With experiences in Europe, North America, and Australia, it's a gift and a memory they'll always treasure.

Huntermoss offers guided and self-guided tours and weekend getaways, so there's an experience for everyone who has the means. They'll get to choose from driving a selection of supercars on the world's best roads, enjoying VIP hospitality at F1 races, or strapping into a race car to conquer iconic circuits like Nürburgring and Spa. Huntermoss also offers a bespoke travel-management service, so let your imagination run wild in creating your dream driving holiday. Lavish accommodations, gourmet dining, and handpicked lifestyle experiences complete this bucket-list journey.

If your favorite auto lover is a racing fan, VRBO offers dozens of trackside and track-adjacent rental properties around the world, including this incredible first-turn luxury condo at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

First, buy tickets to any race at StubHub for the best deals, then check out the local listings near the track at VRBO (do this well in advance to get a great deal) and book a vacation property close to or on the track.

Whether you're looking into NASCAR, MotoGP, Formula 1, or even IndyCar and IMSA races, simply book a home in Daytona, Laguna Seca, Bristol, COTA, or anywhere else through VRBO and avoid the hassle of the hotel hustle. It's way more comfortable and lets you and your friends make the most of your visit.

Giftory is another "experience gifting" site that lets you buy gift certificates for all kinds of driving experiences in hundreds of locations worldwide. The NASCAR Ride-Along Experience is available at more than 10 NASCAR racetracks in the U.S., so your favorite driver can choose a track close to home or at a legendary course such as Daytona.

Like Tinggly, Giftory offers hundreds of experiences all around the world, including dozens of driving experiences such as UTV adventures in Moab and snowmobiling excursions to see the Northern Lights.

Porsche enthusiasts will feel the thrill behind the wheel of classic and legendary Porsches at Porsche Driving Experience locations all over the U.S. Whether it's a Driver Development Course in Atlanta or Los Angeles or a Track Experience at Laguna Seca or Birmingham, there's something for every Porsche lover. There are even Travel Experiences that let your favorite Porsche driver tour with like-minded Porsche fans.

For the Porsche enthusiast who demands the best, opt for the Porsche Track Experience in Europe. Once-in-a-lifetime opportunities include introductory courses to GT track days to the top-of-the-line Rennsport Academy.

One of the most renowned driving and racing experiences in the world, Skip Barber offers one- and three-day Racing Schools behind the wheel of either a modified GT car or an FIA homologated monocoque paired with a 160-hp turbocharged four-cylinder engine at a variety of tracks all over the U.S. For experienced drivers, there are also two-day Advanced schools in both cars. (We reviewed the Skip Barber experience back in 2018, shortly after the company changed hands; you can read about that here.)

Skip Barber's renowned Driving Academy makes a great gift for drivers of all skill levels, particularly young or new drivers who need to hone their skills and tactics behind the wheel.

Just outside Phoenix, Arizona, lies one of the nation's top driving and racing schools. Radford is renowned for its top-flight educational programs, helping drivers reach their maximum potential behind the wheel.

Sponsored by Dodge, Radford offers multiple programs and experiences for drivers of all skill levels in Challengers, Hellcats, SRTs, and more, including driving and racing schools at multiple skill levels and at numerous price points—even drag racing and private instruction.

Racing's number-one oil and fluids brand also runs a marvelous racing school at locations all over the country. If your favorite auto enthusiast has racing aspirations, then this is the ultimate gift idea.

Lucas Oil School of Racing isn't intended to be a casual vacation experience or even necessarily a "fun" activity—although it certainly is that! LOSR is a serious racing school designed to develop aspiring race-car drivers, and its top graduates often move on to professional racing ladders such as IndyCar and IMSA.

With Basic, Basic+, Advanced, and Championship levels, students compete on a level field with other talented up-and-coming drivers in Ray Formula GR11 race cars. These championship-winning cars are adapted to the rigors of a racing school and arrive-and-drive race series, with an extra-large cockpit, adjustable pedal box, and adjustable seat. Courses take place year-round at tracks such as Sebring, Laguna Seca, Mid-Ohio, and VIR. See the complete 2026 calendar here.

Outfitted with a fleet of all-wheel-drive turbocharged Subaru WRX STIs and rear-wheel-drive Subaru BRZs, DirtFish offers the excitement of rally racing to drivers with half-day, full-day, and three-day courses suitable for all drivers. It's an awesome gift idea for auto enthusiasts, and it's perfect for corporate events and groups.

Some sellers allow exchanges or let the recipient choose from a broader collection of experiences. Check the exchange policy and any price difference rules before buying; flexibility can make a specific driving gift easier to give with confidence.

Often. Many experiences offer instant email delivery, and some sellers also offer a printed voucher or gift box. Tinggly says its physical gift box includes a voucher and booking information; options vary by product.

Confirm where the experience takes place, how far the recipient would need to travel, what the voucher includes, and whether there are extra costs for booking, upgrades, or photos. Also check age and license requirements, available dates, cancellation terms, and voucher expiration.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

#4518. Critically endangered tortoises slurp up pumpkin soup

Published Nov 12, 2026 2:00 PM EST

‘Tis the season for pumpkin: the “Superbowl of Pumpkin Weigh Offs,” pumpkin spice lattes, and prepping Thanksgiving feasts. One group of endangered tortoises are enjoying the season with a soup served inside a pumpkin bowl

The trio of critically endangered Asian giant tortoises (Manouria emys phayrei) at the Turtle Survival Center (TSC) in South Carolina recently feasted on this specially made soup with gusto.

“Pumpkin is a great seasonal addition for the turtles,” keeper Carly Sprott tells Popular Science. “It helps keep them hydrated, contains vitamins A and C, as well as fiber that aids in digestion. It is not something we would feed turtles as their entire meal very often, instead we offer balanced meals of fresh salads and various proteins depending on the species’ needs. They were absolutely thrilled when they received a taste of one of their favorite fall snacks!”

In the wild, Asian giant tortoises are found in tropical and subtropical mountainous evergreen forests in parts of Bangladesh and Indonesia. These freshwater turtles are listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, and their primary threats are habitat destruction, collection for local consumption, and collection for pet and food trades. Freshwater turtles like these help their ecosystems by dispersing seeds after eating local plants, dig burrows that other animals in the area can use as shelter, and maintain some balance in the food chain. They also eat plenty of algae and invasive plants, which then improves water quality.

These particular Asian giant tortoises were the first turtles brought into the rescue center in 2013. They were taken from the wild legally in the 1990s, before there were stricter regulations regarding turtle conservation. While the team at the TSC does not name the hundreds of turtles living there, these three do have names since they were the center’s first turtles. They are named Emy-Sue, Emy-Jane, and Emy-Phay, which comes from the Asian giant tortoises’ scientific name—Manouria emys phayrei.

To make things fun, the team creates seasonal treats like these pumpkin soups. In the summer, they will hollow out watermelons. “They love to eat and always follow us around the enclosure to see if they will be awarded an extra treat,” Sprott says.

When they are not eating soup, they spend their days soaking in fresh water pools, warming underneath heat lamps, and roaming around in their large outdoor space.

The TSC is home to 27 turtle and tortoise species, including some of the world’s most endangered that need help.

“Currently, over half of all turtle species in the world are threatened with extinction. These captivating reptiles need our support,” says Sprott . “A few things the community can do to help include cleaning up litter that washes into waterways, supporting local conservation efforts, and treating wildlife with respect in their natural habitats.”

#4517. Tested: The 2027 BMW i7 60 xDrive Exemplifies EV Luxury

BMW’s largest executive sedan remains well suited to battery-electric power.

Taking a classic nameplate and turning it electric is a gamble for most automakers. For BMW, offering identical versions of the same model with gas-powered and all-electric powertrains has become a familiar formula. First launched in 2023, the BMW i7 has already earned plenty of love because of its smooth and silent demeanor. Can an all-new interior design philosophy cement its legacy?

Our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

The BMW i7’s core blueprint is unchanged for 2027, but the new front end is obvious at first glance. More handsome horizontal grille slats connect a still-oversized kidney grille, while extended LED taillights connect the rear end. Inside, the BMW i7 features an updated operating system, a sleek panoramic display, and a dose of Neue Klasse styling.

Powertrain layout: 1 rear electric motor, 1 front electric motor

The mission of an extended-wheelbase executive sedan is poise, and the BMW i7 succeeds at delivering a soothing experience. Yet, powered by a 112.5-kWh battery pack, the i7 60 xDrive is also plenty fast. With 536 horsepower and 549 lb-ft of torque on tap, the i7 60 xDrive offered a surprising punch of performance.

Acceleration was swift—my experience matching BMW’s claim of a 4.6-second 0 to 60 mph—yet also dignified. Using a rear-biased, dual-electric-motor setup, the i7 doled out power in a more linear fashion than most electric vehicles. Peak torque arrived instantly and offered a genuine punch off the line, but I appreciated the more subtle wave of urge available at half-throttle and higher speeds. It felt quick enough to escape an entourage of paparazzi, but not so fast that an executive would be jostled in the rear seat by acceleration. A piped-in, synthesized sound that accompanied hard acceleration was the only sonic nod to speed.

At 6000 pounds, the BMW i7 is heavy. Even with BMW’s full suite of adaptive chassis control systems, including full air suspension and active roll stabilization, the i7 displayed its weight while winding through Orange County’s Ortega Highway. Akin to my experience in BMW’s new iX5, the electric sedan behaved appropriately but was clearly making full use of its electronic dynamic aids. Turn-in was quick enough and the steering weighted up nicely, but I could feel the active roll stabilization fighting to keep the front end pointed the right way. Similarly, midcorner bumps tended to unsettle the rear end into a quickly corrected side step. Steering feel was nowhere to be found either. But in a modern BMW, that’s no surprise, sadly.

Open highway miles were the i7’s comfort zone during my drive. The same heft that made the i7 uncertain in the canyons aided a silken ride, even on California’s disjointed highways. Like the 740, the i7 can decouple its roll bars to reduce unwanted in-cabin movement at higher speeds, and the suspension trick worked well in practice. The i7 felt soft yet secure even at a rapid cruise. Similarly, the 126.6-inch-wheelbase sedan belied its size around town, maneuvering confidently into tight parking spots and narrow urban alleys thanks to standard rear-wheel steering.

Being an EV, regenerative braking did much of the work in slowing this beastly sedan. The mechanical hardware required a stiff stab of the pedal to adequately slow down the Bimmer. However, regeneration kept the three-ton sedan in check while descending, especially when switched into the Medium or High setting.

BMW claims the i7 60 xDrive can do around 350 miles on a single charge. While I didn’t get a chance to charge it, the i7 proved to be fairly efficient during my test drive, reporting a little over three miles per kWh. Even with a mix of highway driving, canyon carving, and suburban crawling, the i7 maintained that efficiency level with little fluctuation.

The 2027 BMW i7 exhibited its biggest upgrades inside. The Panoramic iDrive system is the core of the new Neue Klasse interiors. Gone are physical iDrive controls, instead replaced by a full touchscreen system, operating on a 17.9-inch central infotainment display. An optional recessed 14.6-inch passenger screen is also available for the 2027 model year.

The glamour of BMW’s new system is tempered by a responsive but busy user experience. BMW earns points for adding a scrolling volume control near the nub shifter, but everything else is manipulated through the central touchscreen. There was a permanent menu with obvious icons for climate control, vehicle settings, navigation, and media inputs, but pressing any of these icons only started a multi-step process. Adjusting drive dynamics or climate controls required sifting through multiple menus. Despite these gripes, the responsiveness of the system was rapid, and owners will get used to the navigation over time. Shortcut functions can also be created and assigned.

BMW’s new projected dashboard illuminated necessary information across a span of masked glass on the dashboard, and the placement was nearly perfect for me. The speedometer was placed directly in front of me, while navigation and other secondary information was projected to the right. My only tactile complaint was the oddly shaped M Sport steering wheel. It is better than the four-spoke option we’ve tested on other modern BMWs, but not by much.

My two-tone i7 60 xDrive was appointed with Black Merino leather seats that were heated, cooled, and massaging. The seating experience was comfortable, though a loud fan noise from the ventilated seats was exacerbated in the otherwise-quiet EV. The plush leather seats were generously wide, and the equipped Dolby Atmos system was sonically satisfying. Interior sound levels were exceptionally low, except for the occasional speaker-based acceleration blurt.

The electric luxury sedan is a fairly full market, but the BMW i7 sits at the top of the spectrum alongside the Porsche Taycan and Lucid Air. At a base price of $108,800 (in 50 xDrive form), the i7 meets Lucid and Porsche in the middle. The Taycan starts at $114,250 with significantly more dynamic performance but less interior space. A base Lucid Air is a mere $72,400. For those looking for the benefits of BMW’s new architecture, the all-new i3 sedan offers a sharper driving experience and better range for significant savings but at the sacrifice of the first-class cabin space.

Choosing between a gas-powered and electric 7-series is arguably the harder decision. Battery-electric powertrains suit the luxury-liner mission well, and the i7 offers more power than the currently available gasoline 7-series trims. Further muddying the water is a slim $8000 delta between the base model gas 7-series and a lightly appointed i7. Ultimately, the decision will likely come down to driving range and performance desires.

Adjustable regenerative braking forces can be difficult to get just right, but BMW’s three-prong approach is nearly perfect. BMW offers Low, Medium, and High settings, all of which have distinct levels of braking force, plus an adaptive setting that uses a forward-facing camera to actively adjust retardation levels for traffic conditions.

#4515. Ferrari F40 Driver in Hong Kong Arrested After Nearly Colliding With Double-Decker Bus

The F40’s operator was booked on suspicion of dangerous driving, an offense punishable by up to three years in prison.

It’s almost unquestionable that the Ferrari F40 is one of the most desirable supercars ever made. A big part of its appeal is the absence of features that interfere with the connection between car and driver: there's no traction control, no ABS, not even carpeting. One thing the F40 does have, however, is windows. Apparently, however, a driver in Hong Kong forgot to look through them before pulling out in front of a double-decker bus. His F40 escaped an expensive crash, but he might not be as lucky when it comes to avoiding jail time.

According to Dim Sum Daily, Hong Kong police arrested a 38-year-old man on November 9 on suspicion of dangerous driving. The incident occurred two days earlier on Repulse Bay Road; videos of the near crash began to circulate online, and prompted police to investigate. The video shows the red F40 emerging from a side road, apparently ignoring signs and pavement markings requiring traffic to yield. The driver of the double-decker bus reacted quickly and slammed on the brakes to avoid hitting the multi-million-dollar Ferrari broadside.

Hong Kong Island Regional Traffic Investigation Unit reviewed the footage, and identified the vehicle and suspected driver. Officers then arrested the suspect in the Aberdeen area; police said they intend to pursue prosecution for dangerous driving.

In Hong Kong, dangerous driving is a serious offense. A conviction can result in a maximum fine of HK$25,000—approximately $3200 at current exchange rates—and up to three years in prison. Driving a 478-horsepower Ferrari with a 200-mph top speed and not an airbag in sight demands your complete concentration in any country, however. Thankfully, the bus driver in this situation was paying attention to the road; now the Ferrari driver may have to explain to a court exactly what he was doing instead of watching where his F40 was going.

#4514. BYD and Geely approached FIA about a 12th F1 team, says Ben Sulayem

BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem named the two Chinese automakers while speaking at the New Economy Forum in Madrid, as first reported by Grande Prêmio.

But there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal. The FIA is also pushing F1 toward the kind of engine an EV maker has the least reason to build.

“One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem said of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.

He said he suggested that BYD buy an existing team instead of starting a new one. BYD wasn’t interested in that route. It wants its own team, so Ben Sulayem told the company to come back with a “serious proposal” that shows the project can work.

He also made it clear that Chinese manufacturers won’t get special treatment. Any bid would go through the same process as other prospective entrants, and the rules won’t be rewritten to suit them. Right now, there’s no expansion process at all: the FIA isn’t actively looking for a 12th team.

Still, Ben Sulayem repeated that he’d like F1’s next newcomer to come from China, pointing to the country’s EV technology and the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

This isn’t new for BYD. Back in March, we reported that BYD was exploring a Formula 1 entry, either by buying a team or building one from scratch.

In April, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD had met F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in Shanghai and that an entry was “something we’re discussing.” By July, the tone had cooled. Li said “the dream is always there, but we don’t have a concrete agenda,” and special advisor Alfredo Altavilla set a clear condition: “We will never participate in Formula 1 just to put a sticker on the side of a car.”

Altavilla said BYD would only consider F1 to the extent its technology can serve the sport.

Geely is the new name here. The group sold 3.02 million vehicles last year and owns Volvo, Polestar, and Lotus, a brand with decades of F1 history. It’s also heading into Canada next year as Chinese automakers push hard into new markets.

The last newcomer, Cadillac, took a long road. The FIA opened an expression-of-interest process in 2023, and GM’s team only joined the grid as the 11th team this season, running Ferrari power until its own power unit arrives. Audi got in the other way, by taking over Sauber.

Here’s where it gets awkward for an EV maker. The 2026 F1 power units split output roughly 50/50 between the combustion engine and electric power, with the MGU-K jumping to 350 kW.

The FIA is already walking that back. In June, it agreed to shift the split to 60-40 in favor of combustion for 2027 and 2028. And Ben Sulayem has been pushing for V8 engines running on sustainable fuel with “minor electrification” for the next rules cycle, starting in 2031 at the latest, possibly 2030. Domenicali says F1 should have a package ready to discuss by the end of this year.

So the FIA president wants a Chinese EV maker on the grid, while pushing a rulebook that makes their main strength less relevant.

We like the idea of BYD or Geely in F1. Chinese automakers have the money and the engineers, and they badly need brand prestige outside China. BYD in particular has been on a performance push with Yangwang, and F1 would be the loudest possible way to tell Europe it’s not just a cheap car brand.

they look for visibility/recognition on the world stage, regardless EVs. And in some (primitive) markets they market themselves as hybrids automakers, not as EV automakers.

They will make a hybrid power unit (which they already make anyway) to comply with the backward F1 regulations.

But Ben Sulayem’s comments don’t move things much. There’s no entry process, BYD has already turned down his main suggestion, and Geely’s interest is a name dropped at a conference, not a bid.

A Chinese would likely be good for F1 as well. Motorsports are on the rise in China, and that would be the cherry on top in helping popularize the sport in the world’s largest market.

The bigger issue is the engine. Altavilla was clear that BYD isn’t interested in slapping a logo on a car. It wants F1 to showcase its technology, and BYD’s technology is batteries and electric drive. The FIA’s V8 push goes the other way. It’s hard to sell an EV giant on a sport that’s reducing the electric part of the powertrain.

#4513. Customer busted for using AI image of burnt pizza to scam restaurant

Published Nov 12, 2026 3:03 PM EST

Generative artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented wave of scams, from vocal clone politician phone calls to uncomfortably realistic deepfake images. While most of these are designed and coordinated by groups of bad actors hoping to cast the widest net possible, some are the work of individuals simply attempting to pull one over on specific targets. Many AI con jobs are more convincing than others, but one pizzeria owner in Los Angeles almost immediately suspected a recent patron’s complaint once they saw the supposed “evidence.”

After receiving their pizza from Masa of Echo Park via DoorDash, a customer named “Dana B” demanded a full refund for what they claimed was an inedible, burnt pie. Accompanying their grammatically questionable message was a picture of what appeared to be a charred Chicago-style pizza.

“its burnt to heck. burnt. black. cant eat it. dont wanna eat cancer…,” they wrote in their complaint.

However, Masa owner Rhonda Reynolds knew almost instantly that the allegation was categorically false.

“It was impossible. It was absolutely impossible,” she told local news outlet KTLA 5.

Reynolds uploaded the photo into an app called “Is This AI,” which offered a 96 percent certainty that the picture was faked. She even checked the restaurant’s kitchen security footage to be sure. The footage showed an employee boxing a clearly uncharred pizza destined for Dana B.Masa then laid out the facts in a complaint that countered the first complaint, and the app soon reversed its automatic refund initially dispersed to the scammer. But while justice was served this time, Reynolds remains worried that the experience is only a preview of AI cons to come.

“If this is a new frontier, we’re not gonna make through to the other side if all of our time is spent [on scams],” she said.

Here’s one we didn’t see coming: the team over at KTM X-Bow is entering the world of off-roading with a ballistic side-by-side. It’s called the Arrow, and it’s a seriously expensive shot across the bow at segment stalwarts from Polaris and Can-Am.

And we mean it when we say this side-by-side is pricey. The standard model starts at $59,800, while the Black Limited Edition goes for a ludicrous $98,600.
